Thanks Lauren — a few notes from procurement/Sales Ops side:

- DPA: Yes, we should treat this as DPA-required given Atlas is a healthcare org and they explicitly referenced PHI. I attached the redwood dataflow diagram for their security view (redwood-dataflow-diagram.png).
- Subprocessors: I'll pull the current public subprocessors list and add the short descriptions (GPU infra, metrics/analytics, file storage). If any of those access PHI we will flag and propose Private deployment or a dedicated contract clause.
- Retention: recommend we propose default retention: logs 90 days, request K/V cache metadata 30 days, customer-managed artifact retention per contract. We should be flexible if Atlas needs shorter windows; that will be in the DPA.
- Billing/PO: Standard Sales policy is Net30 for self-serve hosted accounts; for enterprise pilots we accept PO + 50% upfront for reserved Dedicated capacity. We'll confirm pricing with the AE.

1) Hannah — can you confirm DPA language options (our standard DPA vs. redwood-dpa-template.docx) and whether we need to route to Legal for redlines?

Quick security/compliance input:

- DPA: Confirmed — we should execute a DPA. Use our standard DPA template to start; we can accept reasonable redlines around subprocessors and retention. I attached the template for quick reference (redwood-dpa-template.docx).
- Subprocessors: current high-level list we share: Cloud Provider (managed infra), Metrics/Observability provider, Logging/aggregator, CDN (if used). I'll send the definitive list from Inventory service morning of 4/13.
- PHI: If Atlas indicates PHI will be processed, we should recommend Private deployment or explicit controls (BAA-equivalent protections). We need Legal review for any commitment language on PHI.
- Retention defaults: Logs 90 days, audit trails 365 days (encrypted), model artifacts retained per customer config — default 30 days. We can propose contract-level retention to match Atlas requirements.

Procurement routing: Send their redline/DPA to legal@redwood.com and cc compliance@redwood.com. If they need a PO, procurement should issue PO referencing SOW/Order Form — typical turnaround is 5–7 business days once DPA and pricing are agreed.

Suggested reply to Atlas: Confirm we require a DPA, include the template, attach the dataflow diagram, ask if PHI will be in scope and request their preferred PO terms (Net30 or other). Offer a 30-minute kickoff call to align on security scoping.

-Hannah

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending over the intake spreadsheet and timeline. Quick summary and next steps from our side: 

1) DPA: We do require a DPA for Atlas. Attaching our standard DPA template now and copying our Security/Compliance lead (Hannah). Please let us know if Atlas will provide a redline or if you prefer we send a proposed DPA with Atlas-specific retention/subprocessor clauses.

2) Subprocessors: We'll send a concise subprocessors list (cloud infra, logging/metrics, CDN). If Atlas anticipates PHI in scope, we will flag that and propose either Private deployment or contract-level safeguards — Hannah will follow up.

3) Retention: Default suggestions: logs 90 days, audit trails 365 days, customer artifacts 30 days. We can shorten if Atlas requires — that will be handled in the DPA.

4) PO & billing: Are you able to issue Net30? If Atlas requires a PO to start the pilot, please provide the PO number and contact for the vendor portal; we can accept PO + signed DPA to begin provisioning. For Dedicated/reserved capacity we typically request 50% upfront; for hosted pilot Net30 should be fine.

5) Scheduling: Would you be available for a 30-minute onboarding/security scoping call on 2027-04-15 or 2027-04-16? That will help us finalize the DPA scope and subprocessors list quickly.

Actions from us: Marissa will populate the vendor portal once you confirm the PO contact; Hannah will share the definitive subprocessors inventory on 4/13 morning; I will circulate the DPA template and coordinate next steps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Atlas onboarded.

Best,
